mode: image2image (vanilla CSFF card art as style reference)
prompt:
Use the attached reference images, each for one purpose.
Reference image 1 is the STYLE and SUBJECT reference: match its pale bleached bones, flat posterized colour steps, thin dark ink outlines and muted palette; keep the same kind of bones but NOT its frame of wooden poles.
Reference image 2 is a style reference only: match its flat colour fills and ink lines; do not copy its composition.
Draw a Bone Stockpile for a survival game card: JUST A PILE. A loose rounded heap of pale bleached animal bones (long leg bones, a few curved ribs, knobbly joint ends) lying directly on a small flat oval patch of bare brown earth. Nothing around the heap: no frame, no poles, no posts, no fence, no rope. Seen from a slightly high three-quarter view, the heap filling the lower-middle of the card. The bones are pale cream and tan.
Style: vanilla Card Survival: Fantasy Forest card art: flat posterized colour fills in three or four hard-edged tonal steps (cel-like), thin dark ink outlines, a few small ink hatch and tick marks for texture, muted naturalistic palette, realistic proportions. No soft gradients, no watercolour bleed, no paper texture, nothing glossy, no glow.
Single subject only, comfortably inset from every edge with generous white margin, isolated on a solid flat pure white background (#FFFFFF) that fills every edge of the frame, no cast shadow, no scenery, no text, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame.
Avoid: fence, frame, wooden poles, posts, stakes, rope lashing, boundary, enclosure, crate, box, skulls, footprints, tracks, prints in the earth, grass, watercolor, soft painterly shading, paper texture, photo, 3D render, glossy highlights, scenery behind the subject, grey background, off-white background, checkerboard, transparency grid, text, watermark, signature, logo, border.
